description: From left to right are the CPU, main memory, and disk. Inside the green CPU box, the processor is on the left and the cache on the right. Each neighboring pair (processor and cache, cache and main memory, main memory and disk) has two horizontal arrows, one above the other. The upper arrow points right and the lower arrow left.

Above the boxes, two bent arrows bypass the cache: one leads from the processor to main memory and the other from main memory to the processor. These connections represent reads and writes in both directions.

frames.explanation: As the text explains, the disk stores data long term, and data needed for execution is loaded into main memory. The cache inside the CPU holds frequently accessed data and instructions, reducing the number of times the processor must access slower main memory.
frames.title: Data flow between disk, main memory, and cache

summary: The processor, cache, main memory, and disk work together by exchanging data in both directions.
title: Data flow between disk, main memory, and cache
